783	\begin{lemma}[Combined point measurements]
   784		\label{lem:qld-4-10}
   785		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedPointsWitness}
   786		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedPointsWitness}
   787		\notready
   788		\uses{def:expanded-state, def:expanded-point-measurement,
   789			def:povm-distance, def:symmetric-equivalents}
   790		There exists a function $\delta_Q(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the
   791		following holds. For every $x, z \in \F_q^m$ and
   792		$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ there are
   793		projective measurements $\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting
   794		on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$ such that:
   795		\begin{enumerate}
   796			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random
   797			$x, z \in \F_q^m$,
   798			\begin{equation}
   799				\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
   800				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   801				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   802				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
   803			\end{equation}
   804			\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly
   805			random $x, z \in \F_q^m$,
   806			\begin{gather}
   807				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
   808				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   809				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   810				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a} \,
   811				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
   812				\\
   813				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
   814				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   815				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   816				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b} \,
   817				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
   818			\end{gather}
   819		\end{enumerate}
   820		Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold.
   821		The operators $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a}$ and
   822		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b}$ do not commute in general, so the
   823		products in \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} and
   824		\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} differ and the two relations are separate
   825		conclusions.
   826	\end{lemma}
   827	\begin{proof}
   828		\uses{lem:qld-comm-cons, def:expanded-point-trace-projection,
   829			fact:add-a-proj, fact:agreement, lem:ortho, thm:linearity,
   830			lem:avg-closeness, lem:cancellation, def:povm-distance}
   831		Throughout the proof every intermediate error is a $\poly(\eps)$ function
   832		that may differ from one use of $\approx_\delta$ to the next. For
   833		$\omega = (x,z,r,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q$
   834		and $a, b \in \F_2$ define the sandwich POVM
   835		$\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}
   836		= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}
   837		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}_{a}
   838		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}$
   839		from the binary refinements of
   840		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}; by the approximate
   841		commutation of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}, projectivity, and
   842		Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}, on average over $\omega$ one has
   843		$\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}
   844		\approx_{\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}}}
   845		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}
   846		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}_{a}$,
   847		and a Cauchy--Schwarz chain with successive errors
   848		$\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}^{1/4}$, $\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}^{1/4}$,
   849		$\sqrt{\eps}$, $\eps$ establishes the self-consistency
   850		$(\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \simeq_\delta
   851		(\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$, hence the
   852		corresponding $\approx_\delta$ relation by Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.
   853		The orthonormalization lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho}) then produces
   854		projective measurements $\{\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$ with
   855		$\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b} \approx_\delta \hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}$ on
   856		average over $\omega$. Next, the refined point measurements satisfy the
   857		exact linearity
   858		$\sum_{b+b'=c} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_{b}
   859		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r'}_{b'}
   860		= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r+r'}_{c}$
   861		(a direct consequence of projectivity of
   862		$\{\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$), which transfers, on average over
   863		$x, z, r, r', s, s'$, to an approximate linearity of the
   864		$\{\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$ in the index pair $(r,s)$ and then to the
   865		$\{\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$. Consequently the binary observables
   866		$\mathcal{O}^{\omega}
   867		= \sum_{a,b \in \F_2} (-1)^{a+b} \hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}$
   868		satisfy
   869		$\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
   870		\approx_\delta \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'}$
   871		on average over $x, z, r, r', s, s'$. Identify $\F_q \cong \F_2^t$ so
   872		that the pair $(r,s)$ ranges over $\F_2^{2t}$, and let $\rho$ be the
   873		reduced density operator of $\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying
   874		the $\mathcal{O}^{\omega}$, so that $\Tr(S\rho)$ is the expectation
   875		value of $S$ in $\ket{\hat\psi}$ for every operator $S$ on those
   876		registers. For fixed $(x,z)$ let $\delta_{x,z}$ denote the
   877		conditional average, given $(x,z)$, of the squared linearity defect
   878		$\lVert (\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
   879		- \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'}) \ket{\hat\psi} \rVert^2$, so that
   880		$\E_{x,z}\, \delta_{x,z} = O(\delta)$; expanding the square, using
   881		unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index pair
   882		shows that, for each $(x,z)$, the correlation hypothesis of
   883		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} holds in the form
   884		$\E\, \Tr(\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
   885		\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'} \rho)
   886		= 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{x,z}$,
   887		the average being over $(r,s)$ and $(r',s')$ uniform in $\F_2^{2t}$.
   888		Since Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} imposes no upper bound on its error
   889		parameter, it applies for every fixed $(x,z)$ with
   890		$\delta := \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{x,z}$ and yields binary observables
   891		$\{\mathcal{L}^{x,z,r,s}\}$, exactly linear in $(r,s)$ for all pairs,
   892		acting on an extension by an ancilla register in a pure state, with
   893		$\E_{r,s}\, d\big(\mathcal{L}^{x,z,r,s},\ \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \ot
   894		\Id\big)^2 \le \delta_{x,z}$
   895		in the state-dependent distance of the extended state; taking the
   896		expectation over $(x,z)$ shows that the two families are
   897		$\delta$-close, in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance},
   898		on average over $x, z, r, s$, the averaged form of closeness being
   899		the one Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} supplies and the only one used
   900		below (Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import}).
   901		% Import obligation (see rem:linearity-import): the ancilla register
   902		% and its pure state produced by thm:linearity may depend on (x,z);
   903		% following the source ("By assuming that |hat psi> has sufficiently
   904		% many ancilla zero qubits, we do not need to extend the state
   905		% further", references/qpbt-paper/
   906		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:832), they are to be
   907		% absorbed, uniformly in (x,z), into zero-state padding of the
   908		% strategy state, so that the L^{x,z,r,s} act on hilb ot (C^q)^{ot M}
   909		% as the statement requires. The source assumes this padding without
   910		% construction; the absorption is an unresolved obligation of the
   911		% import, not established here.
   912		The ancilla register and its state are absorbed into zero-state
   913		padding of the strategy state, an obligation of the import recorded
   914		in Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import}. Define
   915		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}
   916		= \E_{r,s} (-1)^{\tr(ra+sb)} \mathcal{L}^{x,z,r,s}$
   917		for $a, b \in \F_q$: exact linearity makes each $\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ a
   918		projection, and the family sums to the identity because
   919		$\sum_{a,b} \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} = \mathcal{L}^{x,z,0,0} = \Id$, the
   920		latter identity because exact linearity at $(r,s) = (r',s') = (0,0)$
   921		makes $\mathcal{L}^{x,z,0,0}$ an idempotent unitary; so
   922		$\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is a
   923		projective measurement recovering $\F_q$-valued outcomes from the binary
   924		data by Fourier averaging over $(r,s)$. Its self-consistency
   925		\eqref{eq:qld-q-self-cons} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:avg-closeness}
   926		together with the self-consistency of the $\{\mathcal{O}^{\omega}\}$;
   927		the consistency \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} follows from a Fourier
   928		computation that replaces $\mathcal{L}$ by $\mathcal{O}$, then by
   929		$\hat{R}$, then by the ordered product of refined point measurements, and
   930		finally resolves the averages over $r$ and $s$ using
   931		Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}; and \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} follows
   932		by inserting one application of the approximate commutation of
   933		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} into the same chain. Repeating the argument
   934		with the tensor factors on registers $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ and
   935		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ gives all symmetric equivalents.
   936	\end{proof}

   940	\begin{lemma}[Combined line measurements]
   941		\label{lem:qld-xz-lines}
   942		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedLinesWitness}
   943		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedLinesWitness}
   944		\notready
   945		\uses{lem:qld-4-10, def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:consistency,
   946			def:bracket, def:expanded-state, def:symmetric-equivalents,
   947			def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
   948		There exists a function $\delta_P(\eps,m,d,q) = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ such
   949		that the following holds. For
   950		$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ and every pair of
   951		lines $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$ there exists a POVM
   952		$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ acting on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$,
   953		with answers consisting of pairs of polynomials
   954		$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, such that on
   955		average over pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ independently sampled
   956		from the line-point distribution
   957		(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}),
   958		\[
   959			\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}
   960			_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
   961			\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   962			\simeq_{\delta_P}
   963			\big(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
   964		\]
   965		as well as all symmetric equivalents of this approximation. Moreover, if
   966		$\ell_W$ is axis-parallel, then $f_W \in \deg_{d}(\ell_W)$.
   967	\end{lemma}
   968	\begin{proof}
   969		\uses{def:expanded-line-measurement, lem:qld-4-10, fact:add-a-proj,
   970			lem:cool-closeness-fact, lem:qld-comm-line-cons, fact:agreement,
   971			fact:data-processing, lem:pasting, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   972		Define, for all lines $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ and
   973		$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the sandwich
   974		operator
   975		$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   976		= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
   977		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
   978		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}$,
   979		which forms a valid POVM; since the lines measurements come from a valid
   980		strategy for the low-degree test, on an axis-parallel line $\ell_W$ the
   981		outcome $f_W$ lies in $\deg_d(\ell_W)$, and this property is inherited by
   982		$T$. As intermediate consistency relations, write
   983		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet} = \sum_b \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ and
   984		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b} = \sum_a \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ for the two
   985		marginals of the combined point measurement of
   986		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}. Applying
   987		Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} and then
   988		Lemma~\ref{lem:cool-closeness-fact} gives, on average over uniform
   989		$x, z$,
   990		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   991		\approx_\delta
   992		\sum_b (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   993		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$,
   994		and a direct norm computation from this display and
   995		\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} yields the marginal consistencies
   996		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
   997		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$ and
   998		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
   999		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$.
  1000		From items 1 and 3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}, converting
  1001		between $\approx$ and $\simeq$ with Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} and
  1002		summing outcomes with Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}, the lines
  1003		measurements are consistent with the points measurements, and combining
  1004		with the marginal consistencies gives, on average over the line-point
  1005		distribution,
  1006		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \simeq_{\delta_Q}
  1007		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}
  1008		_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a]})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$
  1009		together with the analogous relation for $Z$. The conclusion now follows
  1010		from the pasting lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:pasting}) applied with
  1011		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ in the role of the combined measurement,
  1012		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}$ and
  1013		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}$ in the roles of the two factor
  1014		measurements, $T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ in the role of the pasted measurement,
  1015		$\delta := \delta_Q$, and $\eta := md/q$, the last justified by the
  1016		Schwartz--Zippel bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree})
  1017		applied to the polynomials $f_X, f_Z$ of total degree at most $md$; the
  1018		two hypotheses of the pasting lemma are supplied by the preceding display
  1019		and by \eqref{eq:qld-q-self-cons}, and the distribution over
  1020		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is that of two independent uniformly random lines.
  1021		This gives the stated relation with $\delta_P$ equal to the pasting
  1022		error, a $\poly(\eps, md/q)$ function, and the identical argument with
  1023		the registers modified gives all symmetric equivalents.
  1024	\end{proof}

  1897		classes of equal size, one for each coordinate. The same divisibility
  1898		underlies the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$
  1899		(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist} instantiated at dimension
  1900		$2m+2$), and with it the statements of Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}

  1905		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), which supplies only that $m$
  1906		divides $q$; indeed the two are jointly satisfiable only in a
